Name: 17_llms_llm_chess_ml
Representation: llms, llm, chess, ml, data, programing, level, prompt, concepts, training
Representative_Docs: Chess is not at all comparable to the way LLMs work. Chess is fundamentally different in that the AI is capable of training itself - there's nothing about the chess AI that depends on human input, because we know how to and can easily do so objectively determine whether a game of chess is a win, draw, or loss. This means that an AI can play a game of chess against itself and learn to do things that lead to a win and avoid things that lead to a loss. With a LLM it is different - the AI is fundamentally incapable of training itself, because the only thing a LLM is trying to do is mimic a human. which inherently makes it impossible to function without human input. There is no success state other than that it looks similar to what a human would write and it also will have no notion of when there's a mistake in its training data - if there's any mistake in code it's trained on, it will repeat that mistake without a second thought about it . This means that the AI will learn all kinds of garbage patterns that technically match the data that's in its training set but doesn't work when you need to extrapolate it to try to solve things that are outside of the training data. Chess AIs are driven by trying to win the game, LLMs are driven by trying to mimic humans - and it should really come as no surprise that if you design an AI with the only goal of mimicking humans that it will never surpass humans.. because any time it does anything better than a human, it will treat those things as mistakes too. || I started a programming job right before 3.5 was released.
